The UN Security Council voted in favor of an arms embargo on Houthi rebels and their allies, including former President Ali Abdullah Saleh, to raise the cost of their advance on Yemen. The resolution demands the Shiite group refrain from violence and includes sanctions aimed at controlling terrorism, though Russia abstained, arguing against the inclusion of sanctions. The move comes as Saudi Arabia leads a coalition conducting airstrikes, and Egypt agreed to form a joint military commission to halt the rebels' advance.

A leaked trailer for Zack Snyder's "Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice" was quickly removed from YouTube after showing Ben Affleck and Henry Cavill's characters. The footage, set to premiere in Imax theaters, features Batman and Superman facing off while commentators debate whether the heroes are a savior or a controversy. On Wednesday, Snyder teased the film's release on March 25, 2016, which also stars Amy Adams.

The jury convicted Aaron Hernandez of first-degree murder in the death of Odin Lloyd, sentencing him to life in prison without parole after deliberating over 35 hours. Jurors described the process as grueling, noting they filled multiple notebooks and struggled to reach a unanimous decision, but expressed satisfaction with their verdict and had little prior knowledge of Hernandez or the case.

A third suspect, George Davon Kennedy, was arrested in the alleged spring break gang rape at Panama City Beach. Previously, Ryan Calhoun and Delonte Martistee were charged; Calhoun was released on bond, while Martistee remains jailed. Authorities are pressing charges, and the victim plans to cooperate after being shown the full video of the assault.

The Defense Department announced that remains of nearly 400 unaccounted-for service members from the USS Oklahoma will be exhumed from Pearl Harbor this year to be identified. The effort aims to identify most of the battleship's sailors and Marines, many of whom were killed during the 1941 attack, using historical evidence and DNA analysis. Next of kin were notified starting Tuesday, and identified service members will be returned to families for burial with full military honors.

A 15-year-old girl was detained at Cape Town International Airport in South Africa while attempting to travel and join ISIS. State Security Minister David Mahlobo stated the minor had been radicalized online through social media and reading materials promoting the terrorist group. Officials have debriefed the girl's family and released her into their care as the investigation continues.

A 20-year-old murder suspect, Kenneth Morgan Stancil III, disrupted a court hearing Thursday by shouting profanities, lunging at a judge, and attempting to flip a table. Stancil is accused of killing Ron Lane, a college employee, with relatives and investigators probing whether the shooting was a hate crime given the victim was gay. After being found sleeping on a Florida beach, Stancil was arrested and appeared before a judge on Thursday, where he initially refused a court-appointed lawyer but later relaced, stating he harbors hate toward gay people.

Robert Bates, a reserve deputy sheriff, is charged with manslaughter after he allegedly confused his firearm for a Taser and shot Eric Harris during a chase. Bates maintains the shooting was an accident, telling NBC that such a mistake could happen to anyone, while officials investigate discrepancies in his training records and the broader handling of minorities by the Tulsa County Sheriff's Office.

In Garissa, Kenya, the Madrassa school where Mohamed Mohamud once taught sits closed as students more the 147 victims of last week's university attack. Mohamud, suspected as the "mastermind" of the Garissa massacre, is now believed to command an Al-Shabaab militia near the Somali border. The incident highlights Kenya's growing terror threat, with officials fearing Al-Shabaab is recruiting local youth. Pope Francis commemorated the 100th anniversary of the Armenian genocide by referencing Pope John Paul II's 2001 use of the term, marking a significant shift in Vatican terminology while emphasizing continuity in church policy.

M Adrian Peterson will be reinstated as an active player by the NFL on Friday. The league suspended the Vikings running back in November over allegations he disciplised his 4-year-old son too harshly. Peterson pleaded no contest to misdemeanor reckless assault in November and received probation, community service and a $4,000 fine.

A Tulsa County reserve deputy mistakenly shot and killed a suspect during an arrest at a Dollar General parking lot, believing he was deploying his Taser. Robert (Bob) Bates, 73, thought he pulled out his Taser during an arrest, but instead shot the suspect, who later died at a local hospital. The incident occurred when the task force attempted to arrest Eric Courtney Harris, 44, a convicted felon who sold undercover officers a pistol; during the confrontation, Harris fled and was forced to the ground, where he continued to resist arrest.

Chinese police arrested over 133,000 people and seized 43.3 tons of narcotics during a six-month anti-drug campaign. Authorities also handled nearly 115,000 drug-related crimes and over 600,000 cases of drug use. The crackdown resulted in the deaths of nine officers and injuries to 657 others, while authorities intensified efforts against online drug trafficking and entertainment industry violations.

Jack White announced a hiatus from touring to focus on an exclusive acoustic quartet. The tour will be limited to five obscure U.S. states, with tickets priced at $3 and sold on a first-come, first-served basis at the venue.

CNN reports that UNICEF has been granted rare access to Sanaa Airport to deliver vital aid amid the ongoing conflict between Houthi rebels and the Saudi-led coalition. The airport, previously bombed, is currently under Houthi control, limiting access to the tarmac where aid workers are unloading emergency supplies. With over 15.9 million civilians in need and more than 100,000 displaced, the mission represents a brief, delicate window to deliver food and medical equipment before hostilities are likely to resume.

Tomasz Lazar's photography project captures the haunting portraits of Polish survivors who were deported to Siberia as children during World War II. The images reflect the deep emotional toll of the experience, showing faces marked by tragedy and time, while documenting their stories to ensure future generations learn from the past.

Robert Bates, an Oklahoma reserve deputy charged with second-degree manslaughter in the death of Eric Harris, has released training documents to verify his qualifications. His lawyer, Scott Wood, argues that Bates met all the required training standards, while the victim's family and supervisors have alleged preferential treatment and forged records. The documents, covering 2008 to 2014, show Bates completed one Taser class and qualified with a firearm 10 times, though CNN could not independently confirm their authenticity.

A naturalized U.S. citizen from Columbus was arraigned Friday on federal charges of providing material support to terrorists and lying to the FBI. Abdirahman Sheik Mohamud, 23, allegedly traveled to Syria in 2014 for training with the intent to return home and kill Americans, particularly U.S. soldiers. Mohamud was remanded into custody and faces a potential sentence if convicted.

However, depression can manifest during careers, and while it is treatable, it previously felt debilitating to a pilot's livelihood. This week's pop culture highlights include the release of a new "Star Wars" trailer featuring Harrison Ford and Chewbacca, a viral logic puzzle about Cheryl's birthday, the retirement of model Gisele Bundchen, and ESPN reporter Britt McHenry's on-air car tow m incident.

Warner Bros. and director Michelle MacLaren have parted ways over "creative differences" just weeks before the start of production on the "Wonder Woman" film. MacLaren, who was announced in November, is the first to depart from the highly anticipated DCU, though which Gal Gadot remains attached to star and the June 23, 2017 release date is still intact. The studio will now need to find a new director to helm the first major theatrical film centering on the popular female superhero.

The article discusses the upcoming verdict in the Pedro Hernandez case regarding the 1979 disappearance of Etan Patz. Hernandez confessed to the crime in 2012, but his lawyers argue he suffers from mental illness and cannot reliably distinguish reality from fantasy. While a judge ruled his confession admissible, the case hinges on whether Hernandez actually killed Etan, whose remains have never been recovered. The case has remained central to the Patz family's fight for justice and awareness of missing children, though another man, Jose Antonio Ramos, was previously deemed responsible in a civil lawsuit.

ABC is developing a revival of "The Muppets" at the upfront presentation. Bill Prady co-writes the pilot, with Bob Kushell attached as showrunner. The project hinges on Miss Piggy signing on, as her relationship with Kermit is currently on the rocks. If the pilot succeeds, it could go straight to series, joining Prady's existing work at CBS.

The author recounts a traumatic experience of sexual harassment on a Mumbai train at age 13, which remained unspoken for decades. Decades later, she continues to hear similar stories of women and girls being harassed on local transportation and other public spaces, ranging from molestation to stalking and lewd comments. Canadian actor Jonathan Crombie, best known for playing Gilbert Blythe in the "Anne of Green Gables" TV movies, died at age 48 from a brain hemorrhage. He was praised for his chemistry with co-star Megan Follows and became a heartthrob to fans worldwide. Crombie’s death was mourned by fans and colleagues as a tragic loss of a talented performer early in his career.

Al-Shabaab's latest attack on Garissa University College, which left 147 dead, represents the deadliest assault in Kenya within the past year and a half. The group, affiliated with al Qaeda, has increasingly targeted "soft" sites like malls and universities as its ground in Somalia dwindles, with Thursday's attack serving as a pale shadow of its former power.

Former rap mogur Marion "Suge" Knight was ordered to stand trial for murder and other charges stemming from a deadly hit-and-run confrontation on the set of the biopic "Straight Outta Compton" earlier this year. Judge Ronald Coen lowered Knight's bail to $10 million from $25 million, ruling that defense lawyers called excessive, and dismissed one of the two counts of hit-and-run against him. In all, Knight will stand trial on one count of murder, one count of attempted murder and one count of hit-and-run, faces up to life in prison if convicted

National Park Week, running from April 18 to 26, offers free admission to the 128 U.S. national parks that typically charge fees, including iconic sites like Yellowstone and Yosemite. The initiative, hosted by the National Park Service and National Park Foundation, features events such as astronomy parties, Earth Day celebrations, and Junior Ranger activities, with the public encouraged to share their experiences via the #FindYourPark hashtag.

CNN reports on the affordable housing crisis in Silicon Valley, highlighting families like Nicole paying $1,000 monthly for a one-car garage, while nationally 7.7 million low-income households spend over half their income on rent, threatening economic growth and family stability.

An American citizen was shot multiple times while driving in Karachi, Pakistan, on Thursday. Debra Lobo, a 55-year-old California native, was wounded in the right cheek and left arm but is expected to survive. Police believe the attack was motivated by religious extremism, as pamphlets stating "America should be burnt" were found in her car.

A jury of Rolling Stone's media peers has determined that the magazine's discredited rape story amounted to journalistic malpractice, citing "startling lapses" in basic reporting standards. The report, which sparked a nationwide debate on campus sexual violence, was pulled after an Columbia University investigation revealed Sabrina Rubin Erdely never verified her sole source's identity or gave the fraternity a fair chance to respond.

Jon Cryer reprised his iconic record-store dance from "Pretty on the Outside" on "The Late Late Show," dancing alongside host James Corden. The recreation fulfilled Corden's childhood dream, as he had long wanted to reenact the scene with Cryer, who turned 50 on Thursday. Like many of the film's original fans, both actors are now well into middle age, but the moment still evoked nostritic excitement for viewers.

CNN reports that public outrage over "religious freedom" bills in Arkansas and Indiana caught governors off-guard. As poll watchers, they knew most Americans oppose discriminatory laws, but politicians underestimated business backlash. For many companies, support for discrimination threatens the bottom line; Marriott and others halted the Indiana law to attract LGBT travelers, a market segment spending $200 billion annually.

Ines Dumig's photo series "Apart Together" documents Sahra, a Somali refugee navigating the asylum process in Germany. Dumig was drawn to Sahra's strength and resilience, capturing her journey to highlight the universal feelings of isolation and the search for human dignity. The project serves as both a portrait of Sahra and a broader reflection on the shared human experience of feeling "apart" despite physical distance.

Jarret Stoll of the L.A. Kings was arrested Friday at a Las Vegas resort pool on a drug-possession charge. He was released on $5,000 bail as the Kings launched an internal investigation. The team stated they are "withholding further comment" while the player, a center with the Kings since 2008, faces the charge of possession of controlled substances.

Police in Marana, Arizona, initially believed a shoplifting suspect's gun was locked and unable to fire, but 10 seconds after being informed otherwise, the suspect fired a shot into the air. An officer then used an unusual tactic, driving a patrol car into the suspect to end a crime spree, leading to his hospitalization and subsequent arrest on 15 charges including shoplifting a .30-30 rifle.

Two Delaware boys are in a coma and their father is unable to move two weeks after they fell ill on a trip to the U.V.I., possibly from pesticide exposure. The family was airlifted to hospitals after the 16 and 14-year-old sons suffered seizures at their St. John villa; the father is conscious but immobilized. The EPA found methyl bromide in the rental unit, a restricted pesticide, and is investigating whether the fumigation on March 18 made the family sick.

A suicide car bomb attack near the U.S. Consulate in Irbil, Iraq, was claimed by ISIS. At least four people were killed and 18 were injured, though all U.S. personnel were safe. The blast occurred close to civilian areas, prompting a joint investigation by U.S. and Kurdish authorities.

Over 300 suspects have been arrested in South Africa following deadly attacks on foreigners that killed at least five people and forced thousands to flee. The government condemned the violence, praising police for preventing further bloodshed, while noting the attacks do not represent the views of all citizens. In the past, Johannesburg has been the epicenter of anti-immigrant tensions, including deadly attacks in 2008.

Davion Navar Henry Only, who spent his entire childhood in foster care, was finally adopted in April after a viral video of his 2013 adoption plea captured the attention of a minister's family in Ohio. Despite a previous disruption due to a conflict with the family's son, Only ultimately found a permanent home with Connie Going and her three children, who agreed to adopt him after she reconsidered his request.

Democrats are increasingly focusing on economic inequality as they prepare for the 2016 campaign, but the likely replacement of Harry Reid with Chuck Schumer threatens to shift the party rightward on financial issues, highlighting a tension between progressive populist goals and the realities of campaign finance.

Saudi Arabia has been bombing Yemen for three weeks to prevent Houthi rebels from seeding regional dominance, though the conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis with over 600 killed and 2,000 wounded, while millions flee the country.

Joy Womack, a former Bolshoi Ballet Academy student, has been dancing at the Kremlin Ballet Theatre since 2013. While she performs principal roles near the Russian president's office, she receives a me me salary of roughly $240 monthly, forcing her to carefully budget for basic necessities. Womack attributes this financial strain to the weakening Russian ruble, driven by low oil prices and international sanctions, and she relies on a friend for accommodation and extra earnings from abroad performances.

Six Minnesota men, aged 19 to 21, were arrested for conspirating to join ISIS in Syria. The group plotted for ten months, recruiting each other through peer-to-peer methods. Four appeared in court and were ordered held without bail, while two others were arrested in San Diego after attempting to cross into Mexico. One co-conporator became a witness for the FBI after changing his mind.

Dr. Sanjay Gupta explores the evolving landscape of medical marijuana in "Weed 3: The Marijuana Revolution," addressing its potential to treat conditions like epilepsy and multiple sclerosis while noting the drug's potential to reduce painkiller overdose deaths. He also tackles the stigma surrounding cannabis, acknowledging that his own views shifted after extensive research, and highlights ongoing federally approved studies into its effects on PTSD and brain function.

Ten years ago, Maggie Doyne left her New Jersey home to travel the world. While working with Nepalese refugees in India, she met a young girl searching for her family, an encounter that "changed" her life forever. Witnessing the aftermath of a decade-long civil war, Doyne sold her babysitting savings to purchase land in Surkhet, Nepal, where she established the Kopila Valley Children's Home and School, now supporting over 350 students and roughly 50 orphans.

By now, you probably have an opinion on Indiana's religious freedom law. Some people support companies that are criticizing the law, saying it allows businesses to discriminate against gays and lesbians. Others, like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, are surprised by the backlash and say the law is just like the federal law and 19 other states have. The debate is heated because it mixes religious freedom and gay rights, and also because people question what the law really means.

Fans of Lucille Ball want her statue removed from a park in her hometown. They say the "ugly" likeness does not look like the "I Love Lucy" star. The life-size bronze statue in Celoron, New York, has been been compared to Conway Twitty, the snake from "Beetlejuice," and actor Steve Buscemi. Even Mayor Scott Schrecencost says he does not like the statue, which shows the comic star holding a bottle of fictional nutrition elixir Vitameatavegamin. Yet, it has been a tourist draw since 2009 for Celoron, the comedian's birthplace, attracting visitors who pose with the statue for pictures.

The group seized the camp by storm, flooding the streets with masked men. For over two years, the camp had been besieged and bombed by Syrian forces. Residents woke up to find the militants in charge, and one resident said, "They slaughtered them in the street." The Islamic State now controls almost all the camp.

China has long used a "Great Firewall" to block its citizens from reading Western news or other content it dis approves of. But a new study says China has gone further. It has developed a new weapon called the "Great Cannon." Unlike the Firewall, which blocks things from entering China, the Great Cannon attacks servers outside of China—including in the United States. The study's authors say this open attack will likely anger the international community, and Beijing may have counted on that.

A German official said the investigation into the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash has not found a reason why the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, acted the way he did. Investigators have not found any notes or conversations where he explained his motives. However, medical records show that Lubitz had suicidal thoughts in the past and received therapy. This happened before he ever got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his group will not leave the main cities or the government institutions. He stated that anyone hoping for their surrender is dreaming.

This came after a top Saudi military official claimed that weeks of airstrikes had significantly weakened the Shiite group. The Houthis surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

Twenty years ago, on April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh set off a large truck bomb in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people and hurt hundreds more. It is the worst act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. The event shocked the country with media stories about "attack on the heartland" and America's "lost innocence." The bombing surprised people because it showed that American citizens were attacking their own government in a way that had never been seen before.

If you care deeply about something, would you protest? Make a sign? Join a demonstration? How long could you keep going for, in the face of indifference and inaction?

When more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school a year ago by Boko Haram militants, millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to plead for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people -- from celebrities to world leaders -- voicing their anger via #BringBackOurGirls, one of the top Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The spotlight on the campaign faded.

CNN reports that Barney Frank, a retired congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He entertained a sold-out crowd at the Center on Halsted by sharing stories from his 45 years in public service. Frank is known as the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. When asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, he said he was not aware of the measure and told the young man not to worry about " crazy people."

A brutal attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has left nearly 150 people dead, including students, and dozens more wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while morning prayers were happening, shooting randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab militants claimed responsibility. This deadly attack comes just months after Al-Shabaab militants killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been behind numerous attacks in the region. It has also recruited some Americans, particularly from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is taking down a statue of a British colonialist after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town started a campaign on social media last month demanding the statue of Cecil Rhodes come down, saying his legacy is tainted with racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, the students waited four weeks for the university to act. Yesterday, the school announced the heritage authority had given permission to remove the statue from the campus. The university said the steps are being taken to keep the statue safe while they decide what to do with it in the future.

Syria is a very dangerous place. An opposition group says the number of people who have died there has doubled in one year. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed, according to a monitoring group. One year ago, the count was 162,402. Two years ago, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died.

The United Nations says that more than half of all Syrians are very poor. They need help to survive because food rations are being cut due to a lack of donations.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva was not silent or shy when it came to threatening a woman. According to a criminal complaint, she called the woman and said, "Leave my man alone. Stop looking for him. I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Prosecutors took the threats seriously and charged her with aggravated harassment, which she denies. She is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

CNN reports that a door with a drawing by the artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday. The door's owner, Rabea Darduna, said he sold it for only $175 because he did not know it was very valuable. The door is now being held by the Khan Younis police until a court date is set. Darduna said that when his home was destroyed last summer, he was left with only a doorway and a door.

A Saudi-led coalition is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. Five days into the attacks, the coalition has destroyed most of the rebels' air defense systems and air bases. Saudi Arabia's navy now controls all Yemeni ports, only allowing in carefully watched medical supplies. Locals are fleeing the fighting, and many civilians have been killed.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry after his own fans booed Spanish player Andres Iniesta. He called the fans a "disgrace."

Spain played Holland 2-0 on Tuesday night. Holland's defenders Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored the goals. Iniesta came into the game late, but the Dutch fans jeered and booed him. Hiddink thought the fans should be ashamed.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if their Euro 2016 qualifier with Georgia will be played with no fans in the stands. UEFA, European football's governing body, has started a disciplinary case against the Georgian Football Federation. This comes after fans twice ran onto the field during Sunday's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi. UEFA is also looking at other charges. These include fans setting off fireworks, and safety problems like blocked stairs and locked gates. There were also reports that staff did not search fans properly.

Football agents were left waiting on Wednesday after new rules were announced. Starting April 1, anyone can become an agent by paying a £500 fee for one year. The FA will then charge £250 every year after that. Established agents were exempt from these new rules. The FA was supposed to have a website link for registration, but as of 1pm it was still missing. Mel Stein believes the new rules will "create anarchy." The guidelines changed after FIFA gave up trying to govern agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not been paid for three months. He had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent.

Despite not receiving his salary, Uvarenko says the fans are impressive. He described their support as "unique" and "passionate."

The 18-month contract player says the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at the club.

David Moore, 25, got angry on the road after leaving his home and immediately got stuck in heavy traffic with Rafal Cegielka, 45. Cegielka was pulling his child out of St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Moore then punched the father and smashed his car with a hockey stick while children watched.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This game brought back bad memories of Spain's poor performance in the 2014 World Cup. However, defender Gerard Pique says coach Vicente del Bosque is not too worried about a third straight friendly defeat.

Holland beat Spain 5-1 in the group stage of last year's World Cup in Brazil. That game ended Spain's six-year time as the rulers of world soccer. On Tuesday, Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena. They held on firmly against some determined Spain pressure in the second half to get a 2-0 success.

Ulrike Berger, 44, is barred by a court order from leaving the country with seven-year-old Kaia. Strong winds and dry weather caused a massive wildfire near the south coast. The fire burned through about 70 hectares of heathland—roughly the size of 70 football pitches. It started after several days of storms had damaged trees and shut down roads in the area. Investigators confirmed the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas were destroyed, ranging in size from half a hectare up to 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services were overwhelmed with 600 calls every hour as people celebrated the New Year. Ambulances were stretched to their limit, and in Cambridge, a field hospital was set up to treat drunk partgoers. At the peak, the London Ambulance Service was handling over 600 calls per hour—more than three times the normal amount.

In Manchester, a man collapsed near an ambulance while others walked past eating takeaways. Another scene showed a man slumped in a doorway as women celebrated the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him recover after he was dropped in December. Mignolet was dropped indefinitely by manager Brendan Rodgers because his form was poor. He quickly returned when Brad Jones got a thigh injury. The 27-year-old Belgian told how he stayed positive despite the disappointment. Mignolet made a save during a league match against Swansea last month. He told FourFourTwo: 'I was positive.'

Twitter user Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the ice balls peppering his backyard and noisily plopping into the swimming pool. Footage shows the hailstones coming down at speed, with many cracking as they hit the ground. The U.S. Coast Guard rescued nine crew members from the ship using life boats on Tuesday. The ship was left drifting in the ocean.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked below. His father said the boy most likely fell while sleepwalking. The incident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, the provincial capital of Jiangxi in southeastern China. A hotel worker across the road said she heard a loud bang around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after getting a deep cut to his face. He feels very lucky the skate didn't hit his eye. Miller had a bad scrape across his eye that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. He is left with a scar, but doctors say he did not damage his eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid wants to sign him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal last July, but has had trouble playing at left back. Atletico hope this gives them an advantage, but Luis said he is happy at Chelsea and wants to stay until his contract is finished.

A Reading fan named Charlie Sumner got a three-year ban from football. He ran onto the pitch topless and did flips during his first game at Madejski Stadium last month. Sumner, 20, did four front flips while the Royals won 3-0 against Bradford City. He landed on his back and was stopped by stewards.

A video shows a group of men riding on top of a van as it swerved around a corner. About half a dozen people were sitting on the roof of the vehicle on a road near the coastal city of Salé, Morocco when it toppled on to one side at high speed. Terrifying footage of the incident was taken from a car following the van, which is understood to have been transporting football fans. The video shows the moment the packed vehicle starts to swerve from side-to-side on what appears to be a dual carriageway.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria this May.

The team, known as the "Young Lions," are the defending champions after winning last year's final in Malta on penalties against Holland. To advance to the quarter-finals, they will have to overcome the Dutch again.

This tournament has been expanded from eight to sixteen nations for the first time.

Danny Collinge scored his first England goal against Norway in qualifying.

An annoyed elephant tried to spray a bull with water because the animal got too close. The elephant was relaxing in South Africa's Kruger National Park with its family by a small pool. The bull walked up to the elephant, which annoyed the elephant. In a photo, the elephant squirted water from its trunk to make the bull leave, but missed. Michael Thorpe was convicted in 2006 for showing a Premier League game at his pub in Devon. He spent eight years fighting to clear his name. Yesterday, his conviction was overturned, but he lost his pub in the process.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at their home in Belfast might stop the June game against Romania. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning. The area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. The Irish FA learned about the problem on Tuesday morning. Northern Ireland's Windsor Park had overnight damage to its West Stand on Monday night.

A 20-year-old football fan ran onto the pitch at Reading's Madejski Stadium during a game last month. He did four front flips while the team was winning 3-0. Steards caught him, and he was banned from the stadium for three years.

A BMW driver with five children was arrested after a student was killed while walking to the library. Hina Shamim, 21, died near Kingston University in London. She was from Peterborough and was known as Hyena. Friends left flowers for her, calling her much-loved and charming. She was hit and killed just weeks before her 22nd birthday.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The pair were at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was angry with the girl because she had allegedly been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen in a black top on the right, and the victim is in the center wearing white.

The chief executive of Stoke, Tony Scholes, is hopeful they can keep their goalkeeper, Asmir Begovic, even though his contract is about to end. Begovic, who is 27 years old, has been linked with other clubs. Scholes believes they can match the player's ambitions. He said Asmir is a terrific goalkeeper and they very want to keep him. He added that when a club has good players, it is natural for people to speculate about their future.

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger sent the video to the bus company Ritchies Coachlines to complain. In the video, the driver is seen turning pages while the bus moves. The bus slows down at traffic lights, and the driver moves his head to read better. The company boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver's behavior and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play against Leicester City on Saturday. Reid hurt his hamstring in a game against Chelsea on March 4, but he is back to full training now.

Enner Valencia will not play. He hurt his toe at home in mid-Mouth and is not yet match fit. Allardyce confirmed that Reid, who missed the last two games, is ready to return.

Five days before their wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway. Brittany died at the scene, and John was critically injured. Doctors told the 25-year-old that he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, confined to a wheelchair.

Against all odds, John recovered. On March 24, he helped lead his team to a championship title.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is looking to recapture what he considers his best form in two years after recovering from injury. The Brazil international enjoyed a run of 16 starts in 19 matches from late November - which coincided with a marked improvement in the team's results - until a groin problem in February's Merseyside derby saw him miss 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the defeat by Manchester United immediately before the international break, their first in the league since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Sick of awkward father-daughter photos? A Japanese photographer named Yûki Aoyama has found a funny way to make them better. In the photos, the daughters smile at the camera while their fathers leap into the air and make dramatic poses. The pictures are from Aoyama's new book, which is called "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old who robbed a bank in broad daylight and ran off with £3,000 in cash. The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall, was wearing black clothing, and has greying black hair and wore glasses. The white male suspect was captured on camera inside the bank. Police say no one was injured during the robbery and they are confident the public will be able to identify the suspect.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has lifted Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. The Confederation of African Football had originally banned Morocco from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined the country $1 million. The CAF also asked for an extra $9 million in compensation because Morocco pulled out of the event due to fears about the Ebola virus. Morocco had to give up as hosts of the tournament, which was won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco can compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.

Tom Boyd says Jason Denayer’s successful loan at Celtic means he is ready to play for Manchester City next season. This would make Ronny Deila want to keep Denayer for another year, but Boyd thinks it is a good thing. He believes Denayer’s success will encourage other young players to join Celtic. Jason Denayer, 19, impressed on loan at Celtic this season. He recently got his first cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing people who doubted him. This great season has been up and down for the 23-year-old, who played well in Italy before. England manager Roy Hodgson believed in Townsend, who repaid that belief with a amazing goal at Juventus Stadium. Townsend scored England's equaliser in their 1-1 friendly draw with Italy in Turin on theter night. Townsend celebrated his strike with Tottenham Hotspur team-mates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The purchase was finalized at a special meeting on Tuesday, where the legal team signed papers to buy 726,707 shares for 45 million euros (about 32.8 million pounds). The deal was first announced in January, but two meetings were needed to make it official. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone talks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said the trip brought "very fond memories," despite reports he received death threats before the game.

Conte became Italy's manager in August after the team failed at the World Cup last summer. Since then, Italy has had mixed results. They drew 2-2 with Bulgaria last Saturday, and Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio got injured before a Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibs can catch Rangers for second place. His team, Dumbarton, have played both Rangers and Hibs already this season. Murray believes Rangers will struggle to keep their current lead, and that the gap at the top could change before the season ends.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in World Cup qualifying games. Even though he was on the team list for both games, he did not play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois started instead. Mignolet posed for photos in a pilot's airplane cockpit and posted them on Facebook.

A large rural estate is for sale for £6 million. The property, called Chyknell Hall Estate, is near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. It sits on 200 acres of land and includes a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. The grounds also have a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and its own cricket green. It is thought that the secluded home could attract A-list buyers because the grounds offer complete privacy.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after video showed them harassing a group of students and hitting one man. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. Student Charles Adams recorded the video while he was smoking a cigarette. The officers approached the students while they were waiting for a bus outside the downtown campus.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke their permanent manager. The 39-year-old, who has only lost once in his last seven games, signed a three-year contract. He took the job in February after Allan Johnston left. Locke will speak at a press conference on Friday.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football calendar takes place. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles between them, and Bayern are expected to keep winning this season.

Usually, this match is called "Der Klassiker." However, this time the two rivals meet with 31 points and nine positions separating them in the table. Even though there is a big points and position gap, the game is still as important as it always is when these two clubs meet.

Jurgen Klop (centle) celebrated with his Borussia Dortmund players after their win against Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left stuck at London Stansted airport after easyJet refused to let her on her plane. She only had two pieces of hand luggage, which the airline would not allow. She offered to pay to check the second bag, but she was told only credit cards were accepted. She is too young to have a credit card.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch to the back of the head outside a sports bar. Robson had been drinking and stepped in to break up a fight. The punch was so hard it made an audible crack, and Mr. Potts fell down dead. Robson, who has a history of violent behavior, was sentenced to three and a half years in jail.

Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Arsenal. She hit the ball into the corner while her teammates Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood accidentally ran into each other, causing a confusion at the set-piece.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces solider Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping. However, many people do not realize how much sleep their mind and body need to feel refreshed every day. According to a recent study, 30 percent of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep daily. Professor David Hillman says that people must "pay back" these lost hours to function well throughout the week. Experists say the average adult needs about eight hours of sleep per night, with a healthy range being between seven to nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb. The argument escalated when a woman went into her neighbour's yard and brandished a metal crowbar, shouting racist abuse at a group of men. The men fought back with their own weapons, and a scuffle broke out. The woman shouted, "I don't deal with monkeys. Go on now you f******g monkeys."

Everyone is watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him this summer. Sportsmail writer Pete Jenson looks at the Spain Under-21 defender. Why are English clubs so keen? His buy-out clause is £13.5m. When you compare that to Luke Shaw – a player of a similar age and potential who cost £27m – it would be silly not to be interested. There are also questions about whether he can handle the speed of the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) playing for Valencia earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a man on a green motorcycle. He saved two teens after a 59-year-old man allegedly threatened them with a gun. The stranger used his helmet to knock the gun away, letting the teens run away.

Tim Sherwood wants Ron Vlaar to play well so Aston Villa can avoid being relegated. Sherwood wants to see the fit defender help the team finish strongly. Vlaar was a key player for Holland in the World Cup last year, even though he missed a penalty in a shoot-out against Argentina. This move could lead to him joining Manchester United. On Saturday, Villa will have their captain back from injury as they play at Old Trafford.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa. He plans to build his own team next season if the team stays up in the league. Randy Lerner is in talks with a possible new owner. Sherwood is focused on keeping Villa safe in the league first, before making big changes in the summer.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City next season. However, City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, says his young players are not ready for the first team. This means Denyer might have to return to Manchester City to fill a gap in their squad. Denyer has played well for Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more accurate date before deciding if he needs to sign a new goalkeeper for the summer. Fraser Forster injured his knee during the 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago, and doctors say he could be out for between four and 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a precise timeline yet and considers Kelvin Davis capable of covering for Forster, but he may have to bring in a new keeper if Forster's recovery takes longer.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team missed a penalty chance in a 1-0 loss to Birmingham City.

Birmingham scored first through Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson in the first half. Matt Derbyshire pulled a goal back for Rotherham just before haletime. However, Rob Kiernan handled Matt Derbyshire clumsily near the hour mark, and Derbyshire went down in the box. Referee Dean Whitestone waved away appeals for a penalty, leaving the Rotherham boss visibly enraged as Birmingham held out to win 1-0.

Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrates scoring the opening goal of the game.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear to see. Holland’s national team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying games than they gave up during the whole World Cup qualifying campaign. Even though Guus Hiddink never calls or writes, the Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. But usually, one step forward is followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night, he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month.

The game is scheduled for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18. Ticket prices are £23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for adults and £5 for concessions in the East Stand. Caley Thistle fans have previously complained that the time is too early for the first trains to arrive in Glasgow.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray says the club was forced to leave the stock market because of the previous board's mistakes. He insists the new board's plans and investments will not be affected.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset by their poor start against Italy on Tuesday. Just nine months after the World Cup, England played Italy in a friendly match in Turin. Before the game, hopes were high after seven straight wins. However, England struggled in the first half and fell behind to a header by Graziano Pelle. Rooney, who captained the team, said the players were upset by their first half performance, but the game ended in a 1-1 draw.

Two of Dundee United's fan groups are angry about the club's leadership. They are shocked that 25% of the £6.3 million made from selling four players went as commission to unnamed parties. The groups also disagree with the chairman's level of investment in the club. However, the board says the criticism is wrong because the team has been performing well on the field.

Gary Locke will be confirmed as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. This happens exactly eight weeks after he was asked to lead the team until the end of the season. The Rugby Park club will make the announcement on Friday morning. Locke has signed a three-year deal. On Thursday, the 39-year-old thanked the players who have helped him win over the new chairman, Jim Mann. Locke took charge in February, replacing Allan Johnston on a caretaker basis.

Chinese parents love having child prodigies. Some have 10-year-old children who are already in university, and others have four-year-olds who dance like Michael Jackson. Now, a new basketball star is becoming popular. A viral video is spreading in China. It shows a small boy with amazing basketball skills that would embarrass professional players. The boy is five years old. His name is Mai Zizhuo. He has been shooting hoops since he was two and a half years old, reported People's Daily Online. The video starts with the small player scoring many hoops before dribbling two basketballs.

Bayern Munich will miss David Alaba for the rest of the season. The 22-year-old defender hurt his knee while playing for Austria on Tuesday. He tore a ligament and will be out for about seven weeks. This is a setback for Alaba, who was already out for three months earlier this season with a similar injury. He said he is disappointed but wants to be back for the end of the season.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace the injured Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. The 6ft 7in, 17st-plus Tilse has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year deal and will join the team as soon as paperwork is sorted.
